main_issue: Whether alcohol can be served at the housewarming in the flat, resolved by keeping the drinks in a cooler box outside the front door

A-B.evidence: B said it looked good (T2); A bought the drinks and B wanted them available. Both accepted the cooler outside (T17, T19). They never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C proposed the cooler outside the door (T13) and asked A about it (T15). A replied 'a cooler outside works for me' (T17).

A-D.evidence: D objected to any alcohol at the party (T4, T9) while A had stocked the fridge. D agreed to drinks outside the door (T14) and A accepted it (T17, T21 'that's settled').

B-C.evidence: C asked whether the cooler worked for B's manager (T18). B said 'that works for me' and thanked C (T19).

B-D.evidence: B needed drinks for the manager (T10) while D wanted no alcohol (T9). Both then accepted the cooler outside (T14, T19). They never spoke to each other directly.

C-D.evidence: C offered alternatives (T11, T13). D rejected the kitchen option (T12) but accepted the outside cooler: 'I can agree to that. Thanks, Agent C' (T14).
